classification.difficultyReason: Read the relative centres and horizontal spreads of paired normal curves.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Which normal curve has the higher mean?

spec.description: Equal-height, equal-spread normal curves on one right-pointing horizontal axis. X is left of Y; slanted leaders identify both curves. Ordinary source blue strokes are rendered black.
spec.mathematics: The curves have equal standard deviations, with the centre of Y to the right of the centre of X. No numerical parameters or ticks are supplied.
spec.answerVisibility: Both curves, their labels and the common axis remain visible in the student edition.

answer.worked: $Y$ has the higher mean because its centre is further to the right.

children.label: b
children.prompt: Which normal curve has the higher standard deviation?

spec.description: Two normal curves share a centre on a horizontal axis with arrowheads at both ends. W is taller and narrower; Z is lower and wider. Slanted leaders identify both curves. Ordinary source blue strokes are rendered black.
spec.mathematics: Both curves have the same mean. Z has the greater horizontal spread and hence the greater standard deviation. No numerical parameters or ticks are supplied.
spec.answerVisibility: Both curves, their labels and the common axis remain visible in the student edition.

answer.worked: $Z$ has the higher standard deviation because it has the greater horizontal spread.
